title: AI Engineer
location: North Chicago, IL, US
description:
About AbbVie

This entry-level AI Engineer will work under close supervision to apply developing technical knowledge in Software Engineering and Generative AI, performing analytic, testing, modeling, and development tasks on smaller projects, and independently on larger, more complex assignments. The role will help design, build, and deploy AI-enabled software solutions, including LLM-powered applications, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and model-serving APIs, to meet business requirements.
Responsibilities:
Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, documents methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Support development of AI-enabled applications and fix straightforward defects under close supervision.
Build and maintain components of LLM-based solutions, including API integrations, prompt and tool/function-calling workflows, and basic RAG pipelines (chunking, embeddings, vector search).
Clean, transform, and analyze data with Python, SQL, and data libraries; build simple ETL steps and visualizations.
Execute assigned test cases, including unit tests and basic retrieval or model evaluations, and help reproduce reported issues.
Serve models and AI services through RESTAPIs and containers, prepare simple configuration changes, and follow deployment runbooks.
Track experiments and model versions and support monitoring and CI/CD processes.
Document work and escalation steps in tickets and knowledge base entries.
Learn codebase, development workflows, and platform fundamentals through pairing and code reviews.
Produce reliable technical outputs, follow quality and safety standards (including AI guardrails), document reproducible methods and records, and communicate progress and risks to project leads.
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or relevant STEM certification; or 4 years of equivalent experience.
Problem decomposition, clear communication, reading documentation, collaborating through code review, and explaining results to non-technical people.
Python and Software Fundamentals Core language: data types, control flow, functions, OOP, comprehensions, generators, decorators, exceptions, file I/O, virtual environments (venv, pip / uv)
Data libraries: NumPy, pandas (cleaning, joins, groupby, time series)
Visualization: Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly
Code quality: type hints, unit testing (pytest), logging, PEP 8, packaging
APIs and web: requests, REST concepts, FastAPI or Flask to serve models, async basics
Tooling: Git/GitHub, Jupyter, VS Code, Docker basics
Databases SQL (essential): SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, indexes, query optimization
Relational databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite; schema design, normalization, primary and foreign keys, transactions
Python connectivity: SQLAlchemy, psycopg2, pandas.read_sql
NoSQL: MongoDB (documents), Redis (caching)
Vector databases (AI-specific): embeddings, similarity search, and tools such as pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Pinecone
Data pipelines: ETL basics, data warehouses, Airflow concepts
Modern GenAI Skills LLM APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, structured outputs, tool/function calling
RAG: chunking, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation
Frameworks: LangChain or LlamaIndex (know the basics, but understand what's underneath)
Agents: tool use, multi-step workflows, basic evaluation, and guardrails
MLOps and Deployment Model serving: FastAPI, Docker
Experiment tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases
Cloud basics: AWS, Azure, or GCP
CI/CD basics, monitoring, model versioning

​​Work with the business and BTS functional leads to clearly define business decisions, solution options and recommendations for a given deal based on deal model, size, complexity, risk, and speed to business value.

​​Presenting BTS updates to the function SVPs in the Executive Steering Committee.

Bachelor's Degree with 9 years of experience OR Master's Degree with 8 years of experience OR PhD with 4 years of experience.

​​Experience leading a portfolio of business applications and leading large, complex cross-functional global IT implementations.
​​​Skilled in creating AI agents and tools to reimagine or improve a process or capability. Led and implemented multiple projects that drove speed, efficiencies, and/or cost savings.
​​Strong Project Management, Executive Stakeholder Engagement, Business Systems Applications and delivering complex cross-functional global programs.

Proven ability to design and manage multiple tasks concurrently in a dynamic environment within given timelines.

Excellent/advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills; excellent problem-solving, communication, and presentation skills

The Risk Management Lead (RML) serves as the subject matter expert for risk management and central monitoring in AbbVie’s Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) model. The RML leads the strategic planning, implementation, and continuous improvement of risk management practices across global clinical trials, partnering closely with study teams and Central Monitoring colleagues to cultivate a proactive and sustainable risk-mitigation culture in support of high-quality study execution and regulatory compliance.

Lead embedding and adoption of the end-to-end RBQM model within and across clinical study teams.
Partner with cross-functional leads to develop and implement risk management strategies across therapeutic areas/programs.

Ensure alignment of risk discussions with study plans and global monitoring strategies.
Coach and influence teams in risk mindset, methodology, and process maturity while fostering organizational capabilities.
Analyze quality metrics/data and risk signals across study, regional, and site levels to drive continuous improvement and early intervention.
Monitor risk mitigation execution, track issue trends, and ensure proper documentation, escalation, and communication of risks/issues.
Support inspection readiness, audit response, and regulatory compliance, in collaboration with Clinical Process Compliance and Quality Assurance.
Lead and contribute to RBQM process optimization, knowledge sharing, and best practice dissemination across studies and therapeutic areas.
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, risk-based, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
Minimum of 10 years’ comprehensive experience in clinical operations, with proven expertise in risk management, RBQM, or quality management.
Excellent working knowledge of risk management methodologies (including risk identification, assessment, mitigation, and documentation).
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams, senior management, and drive change management initiatives.
Deep understanding of ICH/GCP, regulatory standards, and clinical trial processes.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills; proficiency with data analysis/visualization tools.
Exceptional communication, documentation, and interpersonal skills.
Proven ability to lead in a dynamic global environment with complex, multi-jurisdictional studies.

AbbVie is seeking an experienced, hands-on Senior Electrical Engineer to develop and support electromechanical medical devices and drug-device combination products. The successful candidate will combine strong electronic hardware and PCB/PCBA design experience using Altium Designer with practical laboratory capability, including soldering, board-level rework, electrical testing, troubleshooting, and debugging. Strong analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuit design experience, including embedded systems, microcontrollers, power management, sensors, motor control, and subsystem integration.

Experience working cross-functionally and with PCB fabricators, PCBA manufacturers, component suppliers, contract manufacturers, and external test laboratories.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to independently manage multiple technical priorities.

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.

Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .

Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.

Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.

title: Policy Lead, California
location: California, United States
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's US & Canada Public Policy team represents Airbnb and the interests of our community of hosts and guests before the legislators, regulators, opinion leaders and coalitions who shape the political and legal environment for our business. We operate in heavily regulated spaces in the technology sector: short-term rental rules are written and rewritten at the state, county and municipal level, and the outcomes directly determine where and how Airbnb can grow.
The Difference You Will Make:
The Policy Lead, California holds ultimate responsibility for Airbnb's public policy and regulatory strategy in the state. This is a senior leadership position accountable for three interlocking outcomes:
Business growth. Protecting and expanding Airbnb's ability to operate across California by securing workable regulatory frameworks at the state and local level and defending against measures that would restrict supply or impose restrictive compliance burdens.
Regulatory affairs. Managing an active, high-volume docket of state legislation, local ordinances, administrative rulemaking and enforcement,  ensuring Airbnb's position is well represented in each.
Brand reputation among policymakers. Above all, materially improving how lawmakers, regulators and civic leaders perceive Airbnb and its host community, and converting that credibility into durable policy outcomes.
The role is as much internal as it is external. You will  lead a team of Policy Managers covering California's priority markets, manage a bench of external consultants and lobbyists, and be accountable for the state's annual policy budget. Equally important, the Lead serves as the central point of alignment between Public Policy and the cross-functional partners whose decisions shape our regulatory position: Legal, Supply, Communications, Marketing, Safety, Tax, and the business leadership for the region. Success requires building consensus across these functions on a single integrated strategy and then driving its execution.
The Policy Lead reports to the US and Canada Policy Strategy Director and works in close collaboration with the Head of Public Policy and the broader policy leadership team.
A Typical Day:
Set and own the California strategy:
Develop and own a fully integrated, multi-year state and local public policy strategy for California, grounded in data, political analysis and a clear-eyed assessment of regulatory risk and growth opportunity.
Prioritize across a large and dynamic portfolio of state bills, local ordinances, ballot measures, administrative proceedings, allocating team, consultant and financial resources to the matters that most affect the business.
Define measurable objectives for the state and report progress, risks and outcomes to the Director and senior business leadership on a regular cadence.
Own and manage the California policy budget, including consultant and lobbyist engagements, campaign tactics such as paid media, research, programs and political engagement, ensuring resources are deployed against strategic priorities.
Lead cross-functional alignment:
Serve as Public Policy's primary counterpart to Legal on California matters, partnering on strategy, regulatory interpretation and compliance.
Work with Supply leadership to align regulatory strategy with growth targets, understand the on-the-ground impact of proposed rules, and shape product and operational responses to regulation.
Partner with Communications and Marketing to build and execute reputation strategies directed at policymakers and the civic audiences who influence them, including narrative development, earned and paid media, research publication and third-party validation.
Ensure that internal stakeholders at every level understand the California strategy, that information flows to those who need it, and that roadblocks and wins are surfaced early.
Drive external advocacy and reputation:
Represent Airbnb at the most senior levels of California state and local government, including legislative leadership, the Governor's office, state agencies, mayors, county supervisors and city councils.
Build and sustain a broad network of relationships across legislative, executive and administrative offices, and with the coalitions, trade associations, labor, housing and tourism stakeholders whose positions shape outcomes.
Deploy the full range of advocacy tools available to a regulated marketplace: direct lobbying, coalition campaigns, host and guest mobilization, economic impact research, paid and earned media, political strategy.
Serve as a spokesperson on California policy matters as needed, in coordination with Communications.
Negotiate directly with government counterparts to secure regulatory frameworks that are workable for hosts and consistent with Airbnb's national and global approach.
Build and lead the team:
Lead, coach and develop a team of Policy Managers and the consultants who support them, setting clear objectives, holding the team accountable for results, and investing in their growth as strategists and advocates.
Own recruitment, performance management and succession planning for the California team.
Foster an inclusive, high-performing culture consistent with Airbnb's core values, and create opportunities for team members to lead projects that stretch their strategic and operational skills.
Ensure consultants and lobbyists are properly briefed, aligned to strategy and delivering measurable value.
Your Expertise:
12 to 15+ years of progressively senior experience in public policy, government relations, political campaigns, public affairs or regulatory strategy, in a corporate, consulting, governmental or advocacy setting.
Deep knowledge of California politics and government, including the Legislature, state agencies and major local jurisdictions, and an established network of relationships across them.
Demonstrated success leading strategy in a heavily regulated or politically contested industry; experience in travel, housing, technology platforms or other regulated marketplaces is strongly preferred.
Proven track record of changing how policymakers perceive an organization or issue, and of translating improved reputation into concrete legislative or regulatory outcomes.
Experience leading integrated advocacy campaigns that combine direct lobbying with coalition building, grassroots mobilization, research and paid and earned media.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional alignment at senior levels, build consensus among stakeholders with competing priorities, and drive a shared strategy to execution.
Senior people-leadership experience, including hiring, performance management, coaching and developing a multidisciplinary team; experience managing external consultants and lobbyists.
Strong command of budget planning and resource allocation in a results-driven environment.
Ability to rapidly absorb complex legislative, regulatory and technical material and translate it into clear positions and compelling advocacy.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the credibility to represent Airbnb before senior government officials, the media and internal executives.
Experience on political campaigns, in public relations or public affairs, or in strategic consulting is a strong plus.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in law, public policy or a related field preferred.
Your Location:
Due to the nature of this position, the successful applicant will need to be based in California to be able to conduct their work. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.
Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:
Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

From the first demand signal at NPI through factory demo conversion, delivery to fixture vendors and stores, and sustaining replacement, this role makes sure the right device, in the right configuration, with the right content, lands in the right place on time, in every region where we sell.
This is a builder role. Today much of demo planning runs on spreadsheets, email threads, and individual follow-up. You will replace that with scalable mechanisms: a single global intake and ordering system, factory-level conversion at scale, documented approval gates, and dashboards that let stakeholders see status without asking. You will look across North America, Europe, Japan, Australia, and emerging markets and find where we can standardize, automate, and remove cost.
Based in Seattle, you are the single point of contact for demo orders from Channel Marketing teams worldwide, and you partner withNPI program and operations teams, Demand Planning, Trade Compliance, Legal/Contracts, Demo Software and Content teams, factories, and a global network of fixture vendors. You will own outcomes that are measured in launch readiness, order accuracy, and cost per unit.
Key job responsibilities
Global Demo Order Management
Own the global demo order process. Channel Marketing teammates in every region (North America, Europe, Japan, and other markets) submit their demo needs to you, and you run those orders from intake to delivery. Set the intake standard and calendar, validate each request against the fixture footprint, repair-and-maintenance buffers, and push back when quantities, timing, or configurations don't add up. Run the confidence progression (low → medium → high) against each program's NPI schedule, lock ASIN-level demand (demo SKU vs. fresh lot), and place final orders with the factory. Keep every Channel Marketer informed through one source of truth showing each order's status, ship date, tracking, and destination, so they never have to chase it.
Factory Demo Conversions
Lead the shift from vendor-performed demo conversion to factory conversion, a step change in cost per unit and speed to shelf. Define conversion specs per device, retailer, and region (content package, network profile, retail configuration). Bring North America to factory conversion for new launches, then extend the model to every region, with a clear migration plan for fixture vendors and stakeholders.
Launch Readiness & NPI Demo Last Mile
Run the weekly Demo Launch Readiness rhythm across product lines: demo experience readiness, content status, software flags, factory build and conversion status, and arrival at fixture vendors. Tie every program's announce date, street date, vendor disclosure window, and fixture in-store date into one plan, and call out risks early enough to change the outcome.
Demo Content, Configuration & Approval Gates
Own the gate before any mass conversion or deployment. Validate that demo content is live and correct in the right demo administration orgs, generate device-specific demo builds with the software team, and maintain default demo configurations for new launches. Run a documented first-article approval (proof of conversion → sign-off → release to mass production) with a full audit trail by device, retailer, region, and content version.
Vendor NDAs, MEAs, Disclosure & Chain of Custody
Own the vendor NDA and material evaluation agreement (MEA) process end to end. Request and route agreements through Contracts and Security approvals, keep a live record of which fixture and display vendors are approved for which programs and what they may receive (pre-release devices, CAD files, product information), and enforce the timing rules that govern vendor disclosure ahead of announce. Onboard new vendors and new product lines as they come up. Track pre-release hardware by device serial number with full chain of custody, and partner with Trade Compliance on cross-border movement and customs.
Prototype, Non-Powered & Packaging Units
Signal prototype availability at each hardware cycle (EVT/DVT/PVT), own allocation and budget, and prevent shortages that block fixture development. Extend the same ordering mechanism to non-powered demo shells, dummy units, and empty retail packaging for displays
Third-Party Demo Components
Own demo power supplies, cables, and other components not supplied by the factory. Manage suppliers, long lead times, and inventory positioning so components arrive with the devices, in every region.
Global Mechanisms, Automation & Data
Design and ship the systems that make this role scale: a structured global intake with auto-populated device data and suggested quantities, automated status reporting, and integrations with roadmap, catalog/ASIN, fixture, and project-management systems. Use automation and AI tools to remove manual steps. Write the SOPs so the work does not depend on any one person, then roll them out region by region.
A day in the life
How They Deliver
• Stakeholders can check order, conversion, and shipment status themselves, without asking.
• Channel Marketing teams in every region submit demo orders through one process and get them on time, in the right quantity and configuration.
• Devices arrive at the correct vendor or store, in the correct quantity and configuration, ahead of fixture build and install dates.
• Cost per converted unit drops as conversions move to the factory, region by region.
• Every pre-release device is tracked by serial number with documented chain of custody.
• Every vendor has the NDA and MEA it needs before it receives devices or information, with no launch delayed by a missing agreement.
• No program is blocked by a prototype, component, or disclosure gap that could have been forecast.
• Weekly Demo Launch Readiness runs on time, on agenda, with clear owners and decisions.
• Write narratives, SOPs, and business reviews (MBR/QBR, PR/FAQ) that drive decisions and earn trust across teams and regions.
• Identify the next mechanism to build or automate, and land it, without being asked.
• Mentor partners and peers on demo planning, and contribute to a culture of documentation and continuous improvement.

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

title: Sr. Regulatory Technical program Manager, Direct-to-Device (D2D), Amazon Leo, Regulatory, Authorization Readiness & Compliance (ARC)
location: Arlington, Virginia, USA
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's initiative to launch a constellation of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to provide affordable, reliable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Direct-to-Device (D2D) is a groundbreaking service that will bring satellite connectivity directly to everyday mobile devices, extending coverage beyond the reach of traditional terrestrial networks. To enable this, the Regulatory team obtains licenses and approvals for space, services, ground-based infrastructure, and the spectrum required to serve customers in each country where Amazon Leo will operate. There is no globally unified regulatory licensing regime for a LEO system like Amazon Leo, and most countries lack established D2D licensing frameworks entirely.
We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to join the Authorization Readiness and Compliance (ARC) team, a sub-function within the Regulatory organization at Amazon Leo. You will own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading implementation of the D2D-specific authorization plans defined by Regulatory Licensing Leads across priority countries. You will work directly with regional Regulatory TPMs, Legal, and Regulatory Licensing Leads to drive execution across FCC, ITU, and country regulators in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions, ensuring Amazon Leo can offer commercial D2D service on day one in every priority country.
D2D is a first-of-its-kind satellite service category. ITU rules continue to evolve, and jurisdictions impose conflicting spectrum and interference requirements. You will navigate that uncertainty, exercising independent judgment to implement the authorization readiness path forward where no clear precedent exists. This role demands technical fluency in Radio Frequency (RF) spectrum allocations, interference analysis, satellite communications, and 3GPP Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) standards. You will lead the implementation of complex license conditions and, in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, translate obligations into precise engineering requirements that software and operations teams can act on. You will also design and build a licensing obligation tracking platform and automated compliance reporting pipeline to manage thousands of license conditions at scale.
Key job responsibilities
•Own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading the implementation of the authorization path, tracking milestones, and driving resolution of blockers across priority countries.
•Interpret complex license conditions across FCC, ITU, and country-level regulators, and in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, convert obligations into actionable engineering requirements for software and operations teams.
•Drive cross-functional coordination with engineering, infrastructure, business, and operations teams to align authorization timelines with service launch schedules.
•Influence without authority across senior stakeholders in matrixed organizations, resolving competing priorities between customer commitments, engineering constraints, and regulatory realities.
•Identify and escalate regulatory risks with clear mitigation strategies to maintain compliance and prevent operational disruptions.
•Provide senior leadership visibility on D2D authorization readiness, launch risk, and country-by-country compliance status.
•Own the regulatory stakeholder relationship with key customers and partners, delivering precise updates on D2D authorization status and maintaining trust through consistent follow-through.
•Set a course in the face of ambiguity to deliver independently, asking the right questions, clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately.
Export Control
This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.
A day in the life
You will serve as the critical link between the Regulatory team and the broader Amazon Leo organization, driving cross-functional priorities with engineering, infrastructure, and business teams, and providing senior leadership visibility into D2D authorization readiness and launch risk. A key part of this role is managing the regulatory relationship with customer and partner stakeholders who maintain high expectations for communication precision, timeline accuracy, and compliance rigor. You will translate complex, evolving regulatory positions into clear narratives, set and manage expectations across competing priorities, and maintain trust through disciplined follow-through. The right candidate will have successfully managed multi-discipline telecommunications program initiatives, possess a well-rounded technical background in satellite communications, and demonstrate excellent verbal and written communication skills.
About the team
The Regulatory team secures and safeguards Amazon Leo's access to radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbital resources around the world, addresses ground infrastructure licensing and regulatory requirements, and shapes the policies and regulatory requirements that affect our ability to deliver on business goals, enabling delivery of broadband and D2D services to Amazon Leo's customers. The organization operates through three sub-functions: (i) Shaping Policy: leads public consultations, advocacy, and rulemakings at national, regional, and international levels to secure country entry, improve licensing frameworks, enable spectrum access, and prevent undesirable compliance requirements on Amazon Leo; (ii) Securing Authorizations: obtains the licenses required across broadband and D2D services and engages regulators to resolve licensing barriers and secure spectrum access and use rights; and (iii) Executing on Obligations: establishes Lawful Intercept (LI) and Law Enforcement Response (LER) programs by jurisdiction, fulfills the spectrum and network related obligations attached to held authorizations, and demonstrates compliance with service obligations. These obligations range from absolute (e.g., LI/LER) to defensible (e.g., certifications, reporting, fees, content blocking, regulator engagement), where failure carries fines, license revocations, service disruptions, and reputational damage.
The team partners with Business, Legal, Public Policy, and Public Relations to execute the strategy, and align with Design, Engineering, Operations, Security, and Business teams to keep the Plan of Record (POR) synchronized with regulatory requirements.

title: Wireless Intelligence Software Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
location: San Diego
description:
Are you excited by the idea of wireless devices that can sense, learn and adapt on their own? Do you enjoy problems where real-time embedded systems meet machine learning? In the Wireless Technologies and Ecosystems (WTE) organization, you'll help bring smart, reliable connectivity to the world through cellular, satellite and Wi-Fi. Our team builds the intelligence behind that connectivity: the scheduling control software that runs on various Apple products, and ML-driven schedulers and models that power wireless intelligence features. You'll design, develop and deliver the next generation of these technologies so that connections stay fast, robust and power-efficient.
Join WTE and be part of a world-class team of engineers working with cross-functional partners to drive innovation in products used by millions of people worldwide. We are looking for talented, highly motivated, self-directed engineers who can work across layers, from embedded scheduling and control software to the ML models that guide it. Our work starts on Apple Watch and extends to iPhone, iPad, Mac and other wireless products, solving everyday connectivity problems at scale. You'll take ideas from research and prototype through to shipping features, and your work will directly shape how Apple products connect.
We are looking for a highly motivated software engineer to join an exceptional development team building wireless intelligence for Apple's next-generation products. In this role, you will develop wireless software solutions used across Apple’s wireless products, combining embedded software development with applied artificial intelligence and machine learning. Your work will include designing ML-driven smart scheduling algorithms for 5G/6G, satellite and Wi-Fi, and integrating them into real-time, resource-constrained embedded systems. You'll take ownership of features end to end, from prototyping and evaluation through production integration, validation and field performance analysis. The role needs exceptional problem-solving and communication skills, strong programming ability, careful attention to detail and a passion for building great products. This position demands exceptional problem-solving and communication abilities, robust programming proficiency, a meticulous attention to detail, and a passionate commitment to creating superior products. You will do well in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, and your contributions will make a clear difference to future Apple products.
Minimum qualifications: MSc in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
Strong foundation in wireless communication systems, such as 5G NR/LTE, Wi-Fi (802.11) or satellite communications.
Hands-on experience developing and applying machine learning models to engineering problems.
Proficiency in C/C++ and Python.
Experience using AI coding tools as part of your regular workflow, with the ability to critically review, verify and debug AI-generated code.
Preferred qualifications: PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
Experience with embedded or real-time software development on resource-constrained devices.
Knowledge of MAC/PHY scheduling, radio resource management, or multi-radio coexistence.
Experience deploying ML models on-device, model quantization and optimization.
Experience analyzing wireless logs and over-the-air performance data.
Track record of taking research concepts or prototypes through to product-quality implementations.
Ability to communicate complex technical work clearly to cross-functional partners and senior engineers.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting quickly as priorities change.

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. Crowe is seeking a Microsoft AI Business Solutions Implementation Consultant to join our growing consulting team. In this role, you will help clients transform and optimize their financial operations through the implementation and enhancement of Microsoft business solutions.
You will work directly with clients to understand their business needs, translate requirements into effective solutions, and support implementations across core financial processes, including General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash Management. Collaborating with cross-functional teams, you will play a key role in solution design, configuration, testing, and user adoption to ensure successful project delivery.

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field.
2 + Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, or supporting Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance or related Microsoft enterprise financial solutions.
Working knowledge of core financial processes and modules, including General Ledger (GL), Accounts Payable (AP), Accounts Receivable (AR), and Cash Management.
Experience gathering business requirements and translating them into functional specifications, solution designs, and system configurations.
Ability to analyze business processes, identify opportunities for improvement, and recommend effective technology solutions.
Experience supporting system testing, including developing test plans, executing test cases, troubleshooting issues, and validating solutions.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and project deliverables.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with clients, technical teams, and business stakeholders.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a client-focused, project-based environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with end-to-end Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance implementations, including requirements gathering, configuration, testing, deployment, and post-implementation support.
Experience developing functional design documents for system customizations, integrations, and enhancements.
Understanding of financial accounting principles, financial reporting, and finance transformation initiatives.
Experience facilitating client workshops, leading requirements discussions, and providing functional guidance throughout the implementation lifecycle.
Experience developing training materials, delivering end-user training, and supporting change management and user adoption.
Familiarity with Microsoft Power Platform, including Power BI, Power Automate, or Power Apps.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance functional consultant certification or other relevant Microsoft certifications.
Experience working in a consulting or professional services environment.
Demonstrated ability to build strong client relationships, serve as a trusted advisor, and identify opportunities for additional business value.
Experience collaborating with project managers, developers, business analysts, and other consultants to deliver high-quality solutions on time.

RESPONSIBLIITIES:
Strategic Finance Partnership

Support the development and execution of sourcing strategies that improve profitability, cost competitiveness, cash flow, and enterprise value creation.

Provide financial leadership and support during supplier negotiations, contract development, and cost management initiatives.
Oversee purchase price variance analysis and value-realization tracking to ensure sourcing initiatives deliver expected results.
Direct financial evaluation of inflation mitigation, supplier productivity, and continuous improvement initiatives across the sourcing portfolio.
Lead financial assessment of supplier concentration, continuity, country, tariff, duty, currency, and geopolitical risks, including scenario modeling and mitigation recommendations.
Evaluate total landed cost and total cost of ownership when supporting supplier selection, sourcing transitions, localization, dual-sourcing, and make-versus-buy decisions.
Working Capital & Value Creation
Partner with sourcing leadership to improve working capital performance through supplier payment term optimization and cash flow improvement initiatives.
Monitor and communicate the financial impact of sourcing-related working capital initiatives and contractual changes.
Validate realized savings and identify risks to value achievement, ensuring financial commitments are accurately measured and reported.
Establish a consistent performance-management framework and executive scorecard for sourcing productivity, cost avoidance, purchase price variance, inflation and deflation, rebates, payment terms, working capital, forecast accuracy, and value realization.
Define common baselines, ownership, timing, and validation standards so that sourcing benefits are measured consistently and reconciled to reported financial results.
Team Leadership & Process Improvement
Lead, coach, and develop a team of two Senior Financial Analysts, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Establish priorities, allocate resources, and ensure effective execution of team responsibilities.
Build organizational capability through mentoring, succession planning, performance management, and development planning.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance reporting, forecasting accuracy, financial insights, automation, and overall process efficiency.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate closely with Operations Finance, Supply Chain, FP&A, Business Unit Finance, Procurement, and Operations leaders to ensure financial alignment and consistent methodologies.
Influence business decisions across functions without formal authority through strong relationships, credibility, and analytical rigor.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or related field.
7+ years of progressive finance experience required; 10+ years preferred.
Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including coaching, development, and performance management.
Experience supporting sourcing, procurement, supply chain, operations, manufacturing, or related functions.
Demonstrated success leading financial planning, forecasting, business analysis, and strategic decision support activities.
Strong analytical and financial modeling capabilities with the ability to evaluate complex business scenarios.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and effectively challenge assumptions through fact-based recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complex financial concepts into clear business insights.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and financial reporting tools.
Experience with financial systems such as Oracle, SAP, BPC, HFM, Essbase, Tableau, or similar platforms.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required to support sourcing priorities, supplier engagements, and team collaboration.
Preferred Qualifications
MBA, CPA, CMA, or other advanced business or finance credential.
Strong knowledge of procurement finance concepts, including total cost of ownership, total landed cost, purchase price variance, commodity and foreign-exchange exposure, supplier rebates, payment terms, and sourcing savings validation.
Experience working within multinational manufacturing or consumer products environments.
Experience developing commodity, currency, or supplier cost forecasting models.
Proven track record of leading process improvement and finance transformation initiatives.

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide
 Serve as the primary point of contact for international outbound movements from the
United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.
 Manage active Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) requests, monitor shipment
milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.
Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.
Working Conditions
Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

Our innovations in robotic-assisted surgery and diagnostics, digital ecosystems, and integrated service solutions are transforming how healthcare is delivered.
To support the next phase of company growth, the Program Management Office (PMO) is establishing a new Global Expansion  team focused on accelerating access to our existing, commercially available da Vinci and ION technologies in underpenetrated price-sensitive procedures, countries and sites of care.  This requires close partnership with commercial leadership, business units and shared services to ensure strategic priorities are translated into scalable business outcomes and global product launches are executed with agility and confidence.
Primary Function of Position
The Director, Global Expansion, is responsible for establishing this new vertical within the PMO, ensuring robust project management execution to scale global commercialization of existing da Vinci and ION technologies in underpenetrated price-sensitive procedures, countries and sites of care, in line with the aggressive roadmaps and targets that are being established.
This role will partner with Commercial leaders, Product Management, Engineering, Regulatory, Finance, Quality, Supply Chain, and Marketing to execute the 3-year roadmap for regional expansion, remove barriers, and align cross-functional resources to deliver committed launch (APL) timelines for various regions as prioritized by commercial leadership. Product Introduction Planning & Readiness Execution
For products that are already commercially available, the PMO Director will:
Work closely with the Regional Leads who define the product launch roadmap into each country and lead the PMO GMA team to create detailed plans to support regional launches.
Ensure plans cover the necessary scope of activity required to achieve APL / launch readiness, with the necessary timelines and resources.
Assess cross-functional resource capacity and constraints needed to support regional launch roadmap. Escalate resource gaps and/or trade offs required to support successful execution
Ensure project risks and constraints are recognized, and mitigation plans are evaluated and carried out.
Manage the PMO GMA team along with cross-functional resources to execute project plans, monitoring progress and removing barriers to their success where necessary.
Provide portfolio inputs and insights to the Regional Leads so they can evaluate roadmap adjustments where necessary and agree to the final plan.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
To support the acceleration of launch (APL) Readiness, the PMO GMA Director will:
Build effective working relationships and collaborate with a range of partners and stakeholders across the business, establishing trusted partnerships at all levels of the organization to accelerate execution, and strengthen cross-functional alignment on shared goals and timelines.
Serve as a delivery partner to Commercial, Sales and Marketing leadership, ensuring launch plans are aligned with commercial readiness, operational readiness and global/regional priorities for market entry.
Communicate timely and clearly so that the holistic portfolio view is understood, along with progress on APL / Launch readiness, and any risks, constraints or priority conflicts.

Business Units - multi-year plans to support product roadmaps.
PMO BU Teams - delivery of specific product changes that may be required to achieve a new market entry.
Regional and Country Marketing - commercial launch planning, and field readiness.

Build a new vertical within the PMO organization, focused on the acceleration of commercially available products into new markets. Hire and develop talent to build a capable and resilient team that can operate in a highly matrixed area of the business.

Develop a culture of accountability and operational excellence that reliably delivers launches on time.
Process Improvement and Best Practice

Build on the work already done to capture the launch readiness checklists and associated activities, by adding more specific details and documenting tribal knowledge, turning it into repeatable processes that can be used by all team members.

Primary Function of the Position
Contribute your technical mechanical , manufacturing, and problem-solving skills to a dynamic team creating precision instruments for the daVinci SinglePort (SP) platform. This highly skilled mechanical engineer will support manufacturing lines for both mature and new products. Responsibilities include providing daily support for existing manufacturing lines, continuous improvement efforts, as well as developing manufacturing equipment and assembly processes for new products.
Essential Job Duties
Sustain and improve existing manufacturing lines: Provide daily engineering support for existing in-house manufacturing lines.
Own and drive continuous improvement of mechanical fixture s and processes to improve product quality, throughput, and cost. Utilize objective data and statistical analysis to inform and drive decisions.
Ideate, prototype, and implement simple, robust mechanical fixture s and tooling designed to error-proof complex assembly steps, take operator skill levels and manual technique out of the equation, and maximize production repeatability.
Lead root cause investigations and drive dispositions for assembly-related defects using Product and Process FMEAs as guidance.
Support quality system compliance including ECO review and implementation, discrepant material dispositions, nonconformance evaluations, and quality notifications.
Troubleshoot, resolve, and document equipment and process malfunctions in compliance with GXP and Intuitive Quality System requirements.
Assist in line transfer and line duplication activities.
Support implementation of design improvements to existing products, including: Provide feedback to Design Engineering on Design for Manufacturability/Assembly (DFM/DFA)
Lead Design Verification and Validation (V&V) builds
Coordinate cut-in/implementation in production.
Provide manufacturing feedback for supplier change requests (SCRs).
Support equipment and process qualification efforts (IQOQPQ and PPQs)
Contribute to the development of efficient manufacturing lines for New Product Introduction for medical devices for the daVinci SinglePort platform: Design and implement assembly/test fixture s to increase repeatability of complex assembly operations including cable routing, plastics joining (e.g. ultrasonic welding, heat staking, snap fit, press fit), metals joining (e.g. laser welding, riveting, swaging, crimping), and general assembly
Develop, document, and qualify (IQ/OQ/PQ/PPQ) new manufacturing and test processes using statistical tools such as Design of Experiments (DOE), Process Capability (Cpk), and Test method validation.
Specify and refine BOMs, workflows/travelers, and detailed work instructions.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g. Production, Design Engineering, Quality Engineering, Supplier Engineering, Project Management) to meet project objectives including Design Verification & Validation and product launch. Examples include building prototype assemblies, training operators, identifying fixture s/ tooling needed and conducting process validation.
Create and revise manufacturing-related risk documents including Process FMEAs, Manufacturing Line Specifications, Equipment Specifications.
Leadership Responsibilities: Leads/participates in continuous improvement initiatives focused on material cost reduction, capacity enhancement, and streamlining continuity of material supply.

Keep the organization’s vision and values at the forefront of decision-making and action.
Required Skills and Experience

Strong mechanical aptitude and fundamentals: Deep knowledge of mechanical design principles, fabrication methods, precise material selection, and surface treatments to optimize tooling performance.
Advanced CAD, GD&T, and Analysis: Strong 3D modeling/CAD experience (SolidWorks preferred), expert application of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T), Tolerance stack-up analysis, and proficiency in FEA modeling.
Foundation in design, fabrication, and assembly process development for complex mechanical assemblies.
Demonstrated understanding of component manufacturing processes such as injection molding, transfer molding, thermoforming, machining, stamping, and MIM.
Technical problem-solving skills with ability to identify root cause and drive corrective action (Fishbone, 8D Analysis)
Ability to employ statistical methods (Cpk, ANOVA, Design of Experiments) in data analysis for process development and problem-solving.
Effective communication skills (verbal, written, and presentation) and comfortable interacting with production technicians, product design engineers, planning, buyers, clinical engineers, and suppliers.
Able to travel periodically to suppliers or Intuitive manufacturing sites.
Required Education and Training
Minimum B.S. Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline. M.S. preferred.
8+ years with a B.S or 6+ years with an M.S of experience as a process or manufacturing engineer supporting products with significant mechanical content.
Working Conditions
Abhility to lift, maneuver, and troubleshoot fixture s and tools
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience in mid-volume manufacturing of single-use devices or complex electro- mechanical assemblies is a plus.
Experience in medical device design controls and manufacturing (ISO 13485) is a plus.
Machine tool experience is a plus.

description:

Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Team
The Incubator within Future Forward at Intuitive is a cross-functional innovation group focused on identifying, evaluating, and developing new clinical opportunities and technology platforms. The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.
Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.

Excellent knowledge of 21 CFR part 820 and ISO 13485

title: Manufacturing Manager
location: Garland Plant, Texas, United States of America
description:
Job Description
The Manufacturing Manager is responsible for leading manufacturing operations within a large, complex food manufacturing facility with 1,000+ employees and USDA/FDA regulatory oversight. This role provides leadership across production operations with accountability for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
The Manufacturing Manager will develop production leaders, drive Kraft Heinz Management System (KHMS) principles, improve operational performance, and build a culture of accountability, employee engagement, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
As a key member of the Plant Leadership Team, this role partners closely with EHS, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, People & Performance, Supply Chain, Planning, and other functions. The Manufacturing Manager will also assume Plant Manager responsibilities and oversee site operations when the Plant Manager is off-site.
Key Responsibilities
Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations to achieve safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, and people objectives.
Ensure compliance with GMPs, food safety requirements, Kraft Heinz standards, and applicable USDA/FDA regulations.
Drive performance across key manufacturing metrics, including OEE, attainment, yield, waste, labor efficiency, downtime, service, and cost.
Lead workforce planning and labor optimization across multiple production areas and shifts.
Champion KHMS and continuous improvement, using structured problem-solving, standard work, digital tools, and data analytics to eliminate losses and improve performance.
Partner with Planning, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, and other functions to optimize production schedules, capacity, product mix, and service.
Own manufacturing cost performance and support budgeting, forecasting, productivity, savings, and capital initiatives.
Use KPIs and operational data to identify performance gaps, establish corrective actions, and communicate risks and opportunities to Plant Leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop production leaders while building a strong pipeline of manufacturing leadership talent.
Foster positive employee relations, accountability, and engagement within a large, union manufacturing environment.
Collaborate across functions to support plant priorities, product launches, operational improvements, and long-term manufacturing strategy.
Serve as a key member of the Plant Leadership Team and provide overall site leadership when acting on behalf of the Plant Manager.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business, Food Technology, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or a related field strongly preferred.
8–10 years of manufacturing experience preferred, with a minimum of 5 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
Experience leading large-scale, complex manufacturing operations, preferably within an organization of 1,000+ employees.
Experience in a USDA/FDA-regulated food manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
Union manufacturing experience preferred.
Proven ability to deliver results across safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, and people performance.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgets, labor, productivity, manufacturing costs, and operational performance.
Demonstrated experience with continuous improvement, structured problem-solving, operational excellence, and transformational change.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate operational data and KPIs into effective action plans.
Proven ability to coach, develop, and empower manufacturing leaders and teams.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and change-management skills across all levels of an organization.
Ability to work flexible hours, including nights and weekends, as required by plant operations.

title: National Account Manager C&U
location: United States of America
description:
Plan and execute the activities of promotion and sales in multiple areas in a given region. Generate, plan, and follow up daily and monthly sales targets and actuals to achieve the sales targets of the region. Support and approve initiation, expenditures, and implementation of investments to meet the company's business requirements. Work in close cooperation with sales force effectiveness and market research professionals to effectively utilize the sales representatives and look for training opportunities and assignments that would enable their personal and career development. Follow up and increase the performance of each sales representative in the region by making double visits and carrying out periodical coaching. This is a first level of sales management.
Job Purpose
​​As a National Account Manager, you will be responsible for a specified channel. This role is uniquely positioned for an ambitious leader who is craving full ownership and accountability for our products and customers within the assigned Accounts. This is not a traditional sales role. We are searching for a candidate who shows a high level of ownership for their business and is adept at selling solutions and has a proven ability to win new business. We are seeking a candidate who is eager to be a leader, influencer and activator with internal and external key stakeholders from the first day on the job. ​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Serve as a key liaison between Kraft Heinz, the Sales organization, and assigned customers and partners, building strong relationships that drive profitable growth within the Non-Commercial Foodservice segment.
Develop and lead channel-specific priorities across K-12, College & University (C&U), Business & Industry (B&I), and Healthcare to deliver quarterly and annual growth goals, increase market penetration, and grow market share.
Manage and develop relationships across GPO/CMC partners, including Foodbuy/Compass, Entegra/Sodexo, Aramark/Avendra, Premier, and Vizient, while identifying opportunities to establish new Non-Commercial partnerships.
Serve as a subject matter expert within the Non-Commercial segment, using market, customer, insights, and sales data to identify opportunities, analyze performance gaps, target potential customers, and develop data-driven growth strategies.
Develop, track, analyze, and evaluate customer and channel business plans based on Kraft Heinz priorities, customer strategies, and external market factors to drive total customer profitability.
Lead Joint Business Planning with strategic and small-to-mid-tier accounts, tailoring programs to customer strategies while aligning with Kraft Heinz business objectives.
Build and manage a profitable sales pipeline, driving conversion of opportunities and identifying incremental branded opportunities with new and existing customers.
Grow assigned customer business through achievement of revenue and profitability targets, share gains, new and core item distribution, and effective management of Customer P&L and EBITDA objectives.
Develop customer selling stories and recommendations using insights, analytics, and market data to support business opportunities and influence customer decisions.
Develop and track Non-Commercial KPIs and sales metrics, regularly communicating wins, performance gaps, pipeline progress, and areas of opportunity during key sales meetings and business reviews.
Prepare and present periodic customer business reviews, effectively communicating business performance, opportunities, recommendations, and forward-looking strategies.
Lead and support contract negotiations, deal creation, customer presentations, and other commercial discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
Guide trade-spend strategy by channel, evaluate program ROI, and recommend or negotiate adjustments to maximize the effectiveness and profitability of trade investments.
Partner cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Legal, Culinary, Marketing, R&D, and other key stakeholders to develop customer programs, new SKUs, sales collateral, and solutions that support execution of business plans.
Support S&OP and forecasting processes, including demand planning and waste-mitigation efforts.
Challenge internal and external teams to think creatively, develop new solutions, and capitalize on emerging business opportunities.
Demonstrate strong financial and analytical acumen, including the ability to build business cases, evaluate ROI, interpret sales performance, and influence P&L outcomes.
Operate with an entrepreneurial, action-oriented mindset, demonstrating ownership, sound decision-making, perseverance, and the ability to solve complex business problems.
Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication, presentation, influence, and negotiation skills across both internal and external stakeholders.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, sales, or related field preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
​Prior sales experience required with a demonstration of major account management resulting in profitable volume, customer penetration, attainment of new business and growth.
​Experience in national accounts sales, restaurant, culinary, and/or distributor industry preferred. Experience within the Education (K-12, Colleges, University) channel preferred.
​Command of business acumen and strong business intuition demonstrated by discernment that not every sales opportunity is equal and a track record of securing profitable volume and walking away from less profitable deals.
​Strong analytical skills demonstrated by previous experience utilizing systems for tracking and recording sales, effective business planning and data-driven strategy for maintaining current and securing new customers.
​Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, demonstrated by effective presentation, influence, and advanced negotiation skills with both internal and external stakeholders.
​Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
​Must have a valid driver’s license and meet MVR requirements.
​Overnight Travel is required, and the amount varies by territory.​
Work Environment & Schedule
This position is considered a Remote based role that can be performed from a home office with expected travel. Additionally, this role requires working a salaried, exempt schedule to best execute against customer and internal expectations.
