location: Muscatine Factory, Iowa, United States of America
description:
Execute and/or coordinate specialized engineering tasks.
Job Description
The  Project Engineer  directs and coordinates exercises functional authority for planning, organization, control, integration and completion of engineering project for the plant or within the area of assigned responsibility by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate supervisors.
Key Responsibilities of the Role
To ensure projects are completed on time within budget or with successful attainment of objectives.
Completes specific phases or aspects of the project such as technical studies, product design, preparation of specifications and technical plans and product testing.
Design, develop, and improve internal processes and processing equipment.
Coordinates activities concerned with technical developments, scheduling, and resolving engineering design and test problems.
Controls expenditures within limitations of project budget.
Prepares interim and completion project reports.
Provide functional and technical support to the factories to minimize production and maintenance problems.
Apply engineering expertise to equipment design, problems solving, and quality improvement.
Participate in committee or task forces where necessary to contribute to company goals.
Support PRC and key support projects as technical advisor or project manager.
In every activity, use the principles of TQM “To do the job right the first time”.  This includes establishing requirements and the process maps necessary to meet the customer’s requirements and all things done right the first time.
Promote TQM through actions and communications to all customers (internal and external), conformance to requirements, to provide quality products and services and provide technical solutions/leadership for the reduction in cost of quality.
Development of project scope, justification, and factory/company impact.
Appropriation preparation including cost estimates, savings, and timing plan.
Development and management of cost controls, asset controls and scheduling controls.
Hires and supervises various contractors in the scope of project manager.  This may encompass all project areas and total up to 50 people dispersed among distinct trades.
The incumbent must maintain a strong back-up source of technical files, vendors, and manufacturers, and engineering groups in order to respond to needs for new packaging methods or to identify technologies/equipment for application in the packaging area.
Evaluate, plan and implement approved projects in he direction of Engineering, Project Review Committee and/or Management Board.
Cost Reduction/Production Improvement; Participate actively in Company efforts to reduce operational costs and improve finished quality attributes.  Develop projects where appropriate to initiate utilization of cost cutting/quality improving technique or equipment.
Analyzing and preparing appropriation request for capital improvement and replacements of inefficient assets, collecting and organizing data for future capital improvements on a five year capital spending budget basis; maintaining and active cost reduction program.
The incumbent must also possess a high level of human relation’s skills to be able to efficiently interact with individuals from varying work disciplines and cultural backgrounds.
Direct and compile capital budgeting; collect future capital project requirements from factory departments and compile into a final five-year capital budget.  Control the currently fiscal year budget to ensure that the current factory needs are met as well s assuring that its needs are well positioned for the future.
Analyze and prepare appropriation requests; prepares and financially analyzes all capital and expense appropriation requests.  This includes new facilities and equipment for factory operating improvements, capacity increases and replacement of equipment.

Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering from an accredited engineering school or related field is Strongly Preferred
3+ years of experience or full cycle Project Engineering experience.
Strong background in mechanical and hydraulic systems, packaging methods, and materials, electronics and computer applications, and electrical systems.
Strong communication skills are required for presentations to factory staffs on technical issues or specific project activity.
Ability to read, analyzes, and interprets general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations.
Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the general public.
Ability to apply mathematical operations to such tasks as frequency distribution, determination of test reliability and validity, analysis of variance, correlation techniques, sampling theory, and factor analysis.
Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
Ability to work to flexible schedule including days, afternoons, midnights, and overtime as needed.

description:

Coaching and development of one direct report

Job Description:

Location: Mars Petcare (North Kansas City, MO)

About Mars Petcare
Mars Petcare is proud to actively recruit, develop, and promote transitioning military service members and veterans. Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity—the chance to leverage the leadership, operational discipline, and mission focus gained during your military career to direct world-class supply chains that produce beloved global pet care brands like Greenies.
At Mars, you will work with real purpose, supported by talented, diverse peers guided by The Five Principles: Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom. We provide the tools, ongoing learning through our in-house Mars University, and professional mobility needed to turn your military service into a rewarding long-term civilian career.
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced Logistics Lead for our overnight operations (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM) in North Kansas City, MO. In this specialized individual contributor and frontline leadership role, you will oversee day-to-day distribution and transportation activities, coordinate with freight carriers and third-party logistics (3PL) partners, manage transactional inventory data systems, and ensure seamless throughput across our evening operating window.
This position is ideally suited for transitioning military non-commissioned officers (NCOs), petty officers, warrant officers, or logistics officers with proven experience leading personnel, managing assets under tight timelines, and directing transportation movements.
What Are We Looking For? (Requirements)
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent level of verified military/professional experience.
Relevant Experience: 3 to 6 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, distribution, or transportation operations, demonstrating the judgment to handle unexpected operational hurdles and advise cross-functional teammates.
Leadership & Supervision: Proven background supervising and directing personnel, equipment, and resources to achieve mission-critical goals under tight deadlines.
Coordination Experience: Demonstrated track record (at least 4 to 6 months) of planning, organizing, and orchestrating the daily work assignments of team members.
Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to brief operational status, communicate clearly with external carriers, and maintain shift accountability.
Partnership & Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build strong partnerships and collaborate across production, warehousing, and carrier networks to achieve shared performance targets.
Shift Availability: Dedicated availability to work the overnight schedule (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM).
Key Responsibilities
Transportation & Distribution Operations:
Provide operational oversight for overnight distribution workflows, serving as the first-line leader for transactional operations in shipping, receiving, and staging.
Coordinate activities of third-party carriers, subcontractors, and freight vendors, serving as their primary operational point of contact during the night shift under an established contract management framework.
Ensure all distribution operations comply with safety standards, quality control protocols, and Mars operating procedures.
Systems & Data Management:
Utilize enterprise warehouse and transportation data management systems (WMS/TMS) to access real-time shipping data, track order fulfillment, reconcile manifests, and manage bill of lading (BOL) documentation.
Monitor performance indicators (KPIs) to spot movement bottlenecks and execute proactive recovery plans.
Stakeholder & Supplier Coordination:
Maintain strong relationships with external logistics providers and internal plant teams, resolving operational escalations and ensuring on-time delivery schedules.
Support client- and vendor-facing communication, handling inquiries with clarity and professionalism.
Team Leadership & Development:
Supervise, coach, and mentor night shift operational associates, fostering a high-accountability safety and continuous improvement culture.
Pursue personal professional development through formal and informal Mars learning initiatives while developing training opportunities for team members.
Military Occupational Specialty (MOS) Crosswalk
Your military experience translating complex mission requirements, managing tight schedules, coordinating cargo movements, and leading teams provides directly transferable skills for this role. Candidates with backgrounds in the following service specialties are strongly encouraged to apply:
U.S. Army
MOS 88N (Transportation Management Coordinator): Direct match for freight scheduling, cargo booking, carrier coordination, commercial transport documentation, and movement control system management [source: 1, 6].
MOS 92A (Automated Logistical Specialist - NCO): Excellent alignment with warehouse data management systems, staging, transaction auditing, and supervising inventory operations.
MOS 88M (Motor Transport Operator - Squad Leader / Truck Master): Proven capability managing distribution lines, coordinating vehicle/asset movements, enforcing safety protocols, and leading personnel under shift deadlines.
MOS 92Y (Unit Supply Specialist - NCO / Supply Sergeant): Deep experience with property accountability, vendor coordination, inventory systems, and transactional operations.
Branch 88A / 90A (Transportation / Logistics Officer): Directly translates to leading operational distribution, carrier execution, contract alignment, and cross-functional team supervision.
U.S. Navy
Rating LS / LSS (Logistics Specialist / Logistics Specialist Submarine - Petty Officer): Strong match for inventory data system operations, shipping/receiving supervision, carrier liaison, receipt documentation, and supply chain accountability.
Rating CS / CSC (Culinary Specialist - Logistics & Provisioning Leads): Extensive experience in perishable goods distribution, inventory tracking systems, vendor receiving, and quality assurance.
Designator 3100 (Supply Corps Officer): Highly relevant experience directing end-to-end supply chains, freight handling, contractor oversight, and operational logistics leadership.
U.S. Air Force
AFSC 2T0X1 (Traffic Management Operations - TMO): Direct match for booking freight carriers, processing cargo documentation, monitoring contractor compliance, and managing inbound/outbound transit [source: 9, 29].
AFSC 2G0X1 (Logistics Plans): Direct alignment with distribution pipeline tracking, timeline execution, carrier coordination, and deployment/distribution logistics.
AFSC 2S0X1 (Materiel Management - Craftsman / Supervisor): Expert background in automated logistics systems, inventory accuracy, and supervising warehouse operational teams.
AFSC 21R (Logistics Readiness Officer): Demonstrated leadership directing intermodal transit, warehousing operations, contractor performance, and shift teams.
U.S. Marine Corps
MOS 3112 / 3152 (Distribution Management Specialist / Distribution Specialist): Directly translates to managing commercial freight movements, carrier dispatch, documentation, and cargo distribution networks [source: 11, 21].
MOS 0431 / 0441 (Logistics / Embarkation Specialist): Proven ability in multi-modal movement planning, load coordination, staging, and cargo manifest reconciliation [source: 3, 18].
MOS 3043 (Supply Chain and Materiel Management Specialist): High-level capability in inventory management systems, supplier coordination, and supervising material handlers.
MOS 0402 (Logistics Officer): Broad expertise managing operational supply distribution, transport planning, third-party logistics support, and leadership.
What Can You Expect From Mars?
A Mission-Driven Culture: Join a global network of over 140,000 diverse and talented Associates united by The Five Principles.
Professional Development: Best-in-class learning and continuous development from day one, including leadership programs through our in-house Mars University .
Comprehensive Total Rewards: An industry-competitive salary, shift differential pay, comprehensive healthcare benefits, retirement savings matching, and an annual company bonus program.

description:

We are looking for a  Cloud Solution Architect – Cloud & AI Data Platform  with deep knowledge in data platforms and analytics to support customers in building secure, scalable, and AI-ready solutions on Microsoft Azure.

Contributes to providing feedback to Unified Delivery Team on VBDs to refine and further develop content.

Addresses customer/partner dissatisfaction with minimal guidance, and may contribute to the execution of strategies to improve customer experience, value realization, and acceleration of transformation.

Helps the customer/partner adopt and use Microsoft product/platform strategy-aligned (cross-solution area) solutions with minimal guidance from more experienced peers. Builds relationships with technical decision makers (TDMs) with minimal guidance, and contributes to helping build the bridge between TDMs and business decision makers (BDMs). Supports interactions as needed with customers/partners' key stakeholders for bridging understanding of security, compliance, operational and risk requirements.
Acts as the voice of the customer/partner, sharing ideas, feedback, insights, success stories and strategic/technical input with Engineering teams, Product Offerings teams and/or internal communities leveraging relevant insights from feedback tools and systems with minimal guidance from more experienced peers. Contributes to the identification of patterns across customers/partners/territories/industries and leveraging them to develop strategic and actionable insights. May present business cases to program managers, with minimal guidance, to influence product roadmaps, decision-making, bug fix prioritization, and own and drive initiatives as appropriate.

Guides partners in developing offerings, practices, products, and solutions. Assists the partner throughout initial customer implementations. Delivers technical enablement. Identifies and focuses on opportunities that align with revenue goals.
Drives growth of solution utilization pipeline with partner by unblocking technical blockers in customer deals. Provides support to partner and sales teams to clarify specific opportunities through proof of concept and technical pre-sales support.
Technical Leadership: Leverages market insights and demand signals with minimal guidance to assist more experienced peers in identifying relevant areas in which to drive upskilling or accreditations based on demand. Demonstrates technical readiness, both depth-aligned to solution area priorities and breadth-aligned to Customer Success Unit (CSU)/corporate initiatives (e.g., security, resilience, AI), and influences less experienced team members to drive their own technical readiness. May act as a mentor, leading readiness and upskilling activities in the team/organization by educating colleagues on technical and non-technical concepts and sharing proven practices.
Contributes to virtual teams (v-teams) around technologies and customer/partner challenges, sharing ideas, insights, and strategic, technical input with technical teams, internal communities across the field, and the larger virtual team across Microsoft using knowledge of Microsoft architectures and their context in the competitive landscape. Demonstrates industry knowledge and helps grow recognition for Microsoft solutions by contributing to presentations and engagements with external and internal audiences (e.g., Tech Connect, Build, Ignite) Supports team members on contributing to intellectual property (IP) and identifying patterns where no IP exists (e.g., Copilot and AI scenarios) to help build scalable and repeatable models. Participates in external technical and non-technical community events (e.g., conferences, seminars, technical meetups, webcasts, blogs, hackathons) that elevate the Microsoft brand and shares learnings across internal teams with minimal guidance from more experienced peers.
Identifies gaps through delivery, communicates those gaps to relevant team members and internal/external stakeholders, and connects gaps and patterns across business and technology areas that drive changes and improvements to products, IP (both existing and new), technologies, and/or processes/practices that enable solutions to scale across customers with minimal guidance from more experienced peers. May contribute to the development and modification of Microsoft's structured frameworks and methodologies.
Other:
Embody our  culture  and  values
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, Liberal Arts, or related field AND 2+ years experience in cloud/infrastructure technologies, information technology (IT) consulting/support, systems administration, network operations, software development/support, technology solutions, practice development, architecture, and/or consulting OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, Liberal Arts, or related field AND 8+ years experience in cloud/infrastructure technologies, information technology (IT) consulting/support, systems administration, network operations, software development/support, technology solutions, practice development, architecture, and/or consulting OR Master's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, Liberal Arts, or related field OR equivalent experience.
6+ years experience in cloud/infrastructure technologies, technology solutions, practice development, architecture, and/or consulting OR equivalent experience.
4+ years experience working in a customer-facing role (e.g., internal and/or external).
4+ years experience working on technical projects.
Technical Certification in Cloud (e.g., Azure, Amazon Web Services, Google, security certifications).

location: United States, Washington, Redmond; United States, Georgia, Atlanta
description:
Overview
The FinOps Controls & Compliance (C&C) team enables the business to move quickly while maintaining trust, accountability, and compliance. We partner across Finance, Procurement, Operations, Engineering, and Corporate Functions to design, implement, monitor, and continuously improve controls that mitigate risk and support Microsoft's strategic priorities.
We are seeking an experienced Controls & Compliance Manager to lead and enhance control and compliance programs across Finance and operational processes, with a strong emphasis on SOX compliance, Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs), risk management, and governance of emerging technologies including AI-enabled business processes and automation.
This role will serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders who are leveraging automation and AI to transform business operations, helping ensure solutions are implemented responsibly, risks are appropriately managed, and controls remain effective in an evolving technology environment.
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in SOX and internal controls, experience with ITGCs and automated controls, and the ability to partner across business and technical teams to enable innovation while maintaining a strong compliance posture.
Responsibilities
SOX, ITGCs, and Internal Controls
Lead the design, implementation, documentation, testing, and monitoring of SOX controls across financial and operational processes.
Oversee compliance activities related to Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs), including access management, change management, system operations, and related governance processes.
Partner with control owners to ensure controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively.
Evaluate control deficiencies and drive remediation plans through successful closure.
Support internal and external audit activities, including audit readiness, testing coordination, and issue management.
Assess the adequacy of controls over automated business processes and system-generated reporting.
AI, Automation, and Emerging Technology Governance
Partner with business leaders, engineering teams, and process owners to evaluate risks and control considerations associated with AI-enabled solutions, automation initiatives, and digital transformation efforts.
Advise stakeholders on control design and governance requirements as business processes evolve through automation and AI adoption.
Assess impacts to SOX and compliance programs resulting from changes in technology, automated decision-making, and emerging tools.
Promote compliance-by-design principles that integrate governance, controls, risk management, and accountability into AI and automation initiatives.
Identify opportunities to leverage technology, analytics, and automation to improve compliance effectiveness and efficiency.
Risk Management and Compliance
Conduct risk assessments to identify emerging operational, technology, financial, compliance, and regulatory risks.
Develop and maintain risk mitigation strategies and monitoring activities.
Analyze control performance, exceptions, and trends to proactively identify opportunities for improvement.
Support governance processes and reporting for compliance and risk management programs.
Business Partnership and Influence
Build strong partnerships across Finance, Procurement, Engineering, Internal Audit, Legal, and Compliance organizations.
Provide consultative guidance on controls, risk management, and governance requirements for new business initiatives and technology implementations.
Influence stakeholders to adopt scalable, sustainable control solutions that appropriately balance risk mitigation and business agility.
Communicate complex compliance, technology, and risk topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Program Leadership
Lead complex, cross-functional compliance and controls initiatives from strategy through execution.
Develop executive-ready reporting, dashboards, and insights on control effectiveness, audit outcomes, risk trends, and compliance performance.
Drive continuous improvement and standardization efforts across compliance programs.
Embody our culture and values

Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.

5+ years of experience in SOX, internal audit, external audit, compliance, risk management, or internal controls.

Experience evaluating controls related to automation, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and digital transformation initiatives.
Experience with continuous controls monitoring, data analytics, and control automation.

location: United States, Virginia, Dulles
description:
Overview
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day and we need you as a Data Center Critical Environment Technician Manager.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I CE Technician Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development for all employees and offers trainings and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Provides assignment and completion oversight of team members for mandatory, technical, and procedural training material. Assigns and oversees procedure development and reporting to team members. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Guides, oversees, and performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines and supports team members with subject matter expertise. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.
Provides and/or assigns team members to provide necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site for all procedure levels of risk (LOR). May take part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Engages to address and resolve circumstances when supplier/vendor work has been stopped to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates and/or assigns team members to coordinate across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. Reviews and approves vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Leads and provides guidance on coordinating activities and establishing associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Ensures troubleshooting completion paths are escalated appropriately and successfully by their team members. Oversees and advises their team members on troubleshooting systems and/or investigates root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Takes part in, and oversees team in the inspection and supervision of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds regularly for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Ensures all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.
Works on complex, advanced tasks (e.g., stabilization, resolution, recovery) independently. Serves as an operations specialist in a major area of operations (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators) and provides oversight and training/mentorship to team members on tasks regarding these subsystems. Demonstrates an understanding of and operates equipment and systems across all disciplines (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Safely and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur, and collects or provides appropriate escalation details or context to support incident management requirements. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides and leads and coordinates emergency monitoring response plans for irregular or malfunctioning conditions. Oversees team during emergency incident management, assigning tasks for corrective repair as appropriate. Communicates directly to leadership, advises the business on the current conditions, safety concerns, and next steps for incident mitigation and/or resolution. Oversees incident detection, analysis, and containment efforts. Serves as technical expert in ensuring emergency operating procedures (EOPs) are consistent with proper incident response.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks utilization and time tracking results for team members, within applicable task management systems. Reviews and validates added required data, documents, changes logged, and procedures upkeep details (related to building management systems and reports) conducted by team members. Guides and coaches team in CMMS usage best practices. Audits and reviews team's data to ensure performance adherence to assigned work tasks. Generates reporting from CMMS for outstanding and ongoing work orders. Generates ad hoc or custom CMMS reports as needed for management. Reviews spare equipment and parts, updates stock, and signal stock replenishment with suppliers and/or coordination with Materials Handling partners.
People Management
Managers deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching, and caring. Model: Live our culture. Embody our values. Practice our leadership principles. Coach: Define team objectives and outcomes. Enable success across boundaries. Help the team adapt and learn. Care: Attract and retain great people. Know each individual’s capabilities and aspirations. Invest in the growth of others.
Other
Embody our culture and values
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
5+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Citizenship Verification:  This position requires verification of citizenship due to citizenship-based legal restrictions. Specifically, this position supports United States federal, state, and/or local  government agency customers and is subject to certain citizenship-based restrictions where required or permitted by applicable law. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Preferred qualifications
1+ year(s) experience in a specialized area (e.g., mechanical field, electrical field, controls field) or related field.
Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education AND 7+ years mission-critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 10+ years mission critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
1+ year(s) people management experience.
Critical Environment Ops M3 - The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $75,400 - $167,900 per year. At Microsoft, we’re building a modern, AI-forward marketing organization that learns faster, activates smarter, and drives measurable impact. We prioritize outcomes over outputs, embrace rapid learning loops, and operate in agile flight formations that unite disciplines across Commercial Brand, Creative, and Customer Marketing.
This role is focused on the intersection of creators, content, and production.
For the last decade, brands treated social media as another channel to fill with content. Today, AI is reshaping how people discover information, create, learn, and connect. As content becomes easier to generate, the people behind it matter more than ever. Audiences don’t follow brands the way they follow people. They follow creators: individuals with a point of view, a voice, and a relationship with their community that no ad buy can replicate. Creators have become the new media companies, writing, shooting, editing, and distributing with a speed and authenticity traditional production struggles to match.
That shift changes what great brand content looks like, and how it gets made. Sometimes the best thing a brand can do is hand a creator a great brief and get out of the way. Other times, the work calls for a brand-quality shoot built around a creator, crafted to look a specific way, then published through their channels to their audience. Most of the time, it’s somewhere in between. Either way, someone has to make it run.
In this role, you will join Creator & Fandom, the team behind Microsoft’s creator and influencer programs, our in-house creator studio, and community programs. As Senior Creator Content Producer, you’ll be the production owner for creator work across campaigns, events, and community activations.
This isn’t a role where you’ll spend months taking notes from the sidelines. You’ll quickly take ownership of real productions that reach global audiences, work alongside creators and talent every week, and help shape how one of the world’s most iconic technology companies makes content with the people audiences actually trust.
At Microsoft, our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. description:
Overview
Microsoft’s partner business depends on trusted, connected data for planning, execution, reporting, and emerging AI scenarios. Partner One Sigle Source of Truth (OSOT) brings together data from multiple authoritative systems and delivers governed data products and insights to partner-business teams and downstream consumers.
We are seeking a technically fluent Product Manager to own the direction and outcomes of Partner OSOT. You will define the product strategy and roadmap, prioritize the backlog, translate ambiguous partner-business needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria, and partner closely with engineers on architecture, data models, APIs, security, reliability, and trade-offs. This is a product-ownership role—not primarily a delivery-coordination or hands-on software-engineering role. Success means measurable customer and business value, trusted data products, and healthy production operations.
Responsibilities
•  Own product strategy and roadmap. Define target users, product outcomes, success measures, and a sequenced roadmap for Partner OSOT. Make explicit prioritization decisions across new capabilities, data quality, platform health, technical debt, and partner-business needs; explain the rationale and trade-offs to stakeholders.
•  Own discovery, requirements, and the backlog. Work directly with partner sales and operations, analytics consumers, data stewards, source-system owners, and engineering to frame problems and validate needs. Write clear product requirements, user scenarios, data contracts or interface expectations, and testable acceptance criteria; maintain and prioritize a transparent backlog and decide when work meets the intended outcome.
•  Lead technical product decisions with engineering. Engage credibly in discussions of APIs, source integration, identity and mastering, data models, cloud architecture, access controls, scalability, reliability, and cost. Evaluate options with technical leads, document decisions and dependencies, and make product trade-offs without substituting for engineering design ownership.
•  Deliver trusted data and analytics products. Shape curated data products that serve BI, reporting, and AI use cases. Define expectations for lineage, definitions, freshness, quality, discoverability, and governed access; use adoption, data-quality, and consumer feedback signals to improve the product.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree AND 4+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience. 2+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience owning a technical product or platform roadmap, requirements, prioritization, backlog, and acceptance criteria, with evidence of decisions and shipped outcomes—not only project tracking or delivery coordination.
Experience working credibly with engineers on APIs, data models, system architecture, cloud services, security, reliability, scale, and technical trade-offs; able to challenge assumptions and explain choices without needing to be the primary implementer.
Experience with data platforms, pipelines, analytics or BI products, data quality, governance, or AI/data-product use cases; able to define what trustworthy, usable data means for consumers.
Experience turning ambiguous business needs into clear user problems, technical/product requirements, measurable outcomes, and phased delivery plans across multiple teams and dependencies.
Experience making product decisions for production services or data products, including incidents, service health, access, compliance, reliability, and cost.
Written and verbal communication experience; able to align business and technical stakeholders, explain trade-offs, and make decisions visible to leadership and delivery teams.

title: Model Policy Manager, Emerging AI Misuse
location: San Francisco
description:
About the Team

The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards.

About the Role

As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond.

This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

In this role, you will: 

 - Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers.

 - Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses.

 - Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse.

 - Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work.

 - Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems.

 - Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others.

 - Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it.

 - Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria.

 - Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next.

 - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures.

 - Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards.

 - Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change.

 - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change.

description:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. About the Role

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability.

 - Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management.

 - Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces.

 - Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing.

 - Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access.

 - Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans.

 - Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

 - You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance.

 - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

 - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

 - You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability.

 - You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation.

location: San Francisco
description:
About the Team

The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity.

Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health.

Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship.

We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models.

 - Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior.

 - Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores.

 - Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians.

 - Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions.

 - Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people.

 - Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely.

 - Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem.

 - Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence.

 - Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one.

 - Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done.

 - Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product.

 - Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research.

 

If you want your work to help make medical intelligence widely accessible—and to work on some of the most important frontier problems at the intersection of AI, science, and human health—we’d love to hear from you.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
location: San Francisco
description:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

About the Team

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.

 - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.

 - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.

 - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.

 - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run.

We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give.

 - Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations.

 - Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models.

 - Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale.

 - Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model.

 - Bring practical security judgment from industry work, a research project, collaboration with a security team, or capture-the-flag competitions. We also welcome reinforcement learning practitioners motivated to develop that judgment alongside security researchers.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Role Summary Rivian is seeking a Senior Staff Radar Antenna Design Engineer to lead the architecture, design, and production maturation of advanced waveguide antennas for high-performance imaging radar systems. This role is for a technical leader with deep expertise in electromagnetic design who can translate demanding radar performance requirements into robust, manufacturable antenna solutions. You will own antenna design from concept through vehicle integration, working across radar architecture, RF hardware, mechanical engineering, signal processing, manufacturing, validation, and suppliers. The ideal candidate combines first-principles electromagnetic insight with strong judgment in system tradeoffs, design-for-manufacturing, and execution of complex hardware programs. Responsibilities Define antenna architectures and performance targets for next-generation imaging radar systems, including field of view, angular resolution, gain, sidelobe levels, polarization, efficiency, bandwidth, scan performance, and calibration stability. Lead the design and optimization of advanced waveguide antenna technologies, including slotted-waveguide arrays, waveguide feeds, corporate and series-fed networks, apertures, transitions, radomes, and RF packaging interfaces. Develop electromagnetic models and design methods for complex antenna structures, accounting for mutual coupling, fabrication tolerances, thermal effects, dielectric loading, surface roughness, leakage, losses, and integration constraints. Drive antenna concepts through electromagnetic simulation, prototype design, fabrication, near-field and far-field measurement, correlation, root-cause analysis, and design iteration. Establish antenna-level budgets, verification plans, acceptance criteria, and correlation methodologies aligned with radar system performance. Partner with radar architects and RF engineers to optimize antenna, transceiver, packaging, calibration, and signal-processing tradeoffs at the system level. Lead integration of the antenna into automotive packaging, including radome effects, bumper and fascia materials, mounting constraints, environmental sealing, thermal management, and vehicle-level electromagnetic compatibility. Own technical decisions and communicate tradeoffs clearly to senior leadership, cross-functional teams, and external suppliers. Mentor antenna engineers and raise the technical bar through design reviews, reusable analysis methods, modeling standards, and measurement best practices. Guide supplier technical development, including design reviews, process capability, tolerance analysis, test correlation, and corrective actions. Support design release, validation, production launch, and field issue resolution for radar antenna hardware. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related technical field, with significant industry experience; advanced degree preferred. Typically 12+ years of relevant engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated technical depth and impact. Extensive professional experience designing antennas or microwave components for demanding radar, sensing, communications, aerospace, or automotive applications. Deep expertise in waveguide antenna design, including aperture synthesis, slotted-waveguide arrays, feed networks, transitions, mode control, impedance matching, and broadband performance optimization. Demonstrated ownership of antenna products from electromagnetic concept through prototype, measurement correlation, design verification, and production release. Strong command of electromagnetic theory, antenna array theory, microwave engineering, scattering parameters, polarization, propagation, and RF measurement techniques. Expert-level experience with 3D full-wave electromagnetic simulation and optimization tools, such as Ansys HFSS, CST Studio Suite, or equivalent. Hands-on experience with antenna measurement systems, including near-field or far-field ranges, over-the-air testing, calibration, pattern characterization, and uncertainty analysis. Experience performing tolerance analysis and designing antennas for manufacturability, repeatability, environmental robustness, and high-volume production. Ability to interpret complex measurement data, identify root causes, and make technically rigorous design decisions under schedule and cost constraints. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence across disciplines without direct authority. Preferred Qualifications Experience with imaging radar architectures, electronically scanned arrays, MIMO radar, high-channel-count systems, or high-resolution automotive radar. Experience designing antennas for millimeter-wave frequencies, particularly 76–81 GHz or adjacent bands. Experience with waveguide manufacturing processes such as precision machining, metal injection molding, die casting, additive manufacturing, plating, metallization, or precision assembly. Knowledge of automotive radar regulatory, EMC, environmental, and reliability requirements. Experience with radome and fascia electromagnetic characterization, material stack-up modeling, and vehicle-level integration. Familiarity with automated electromagnetic optimization, scripting, data reduction, and engineering workflows using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools. Experience developing correlation fixtures, calibration methods, and production end-of-line antenna test strategies. Track record of technical leadership on complex hardware programs and successful mentoring of senior engineers. Published technical work, patents, conference contributions, or demonstrated thought leadership in antenna or microwave engineering. Through research, documentation, and coaching, you help Account Managers learn new products and level up their product knowledge, and you work cross-functionally with Support, Product, and Engineering to solve problems and bring customer insight back to the teams building Samsara. Account Managers continue to own the customer relationship and the renewal; you own the project and the adoption outcome.

Support the broader team in learning new products and upleveling product knowledge through training, documentation, and hands-on enablement.
Work cross-functionally with Support, Product, and Engineering to troubleshoot complex issues, and share customer insights that inform the product roadmap.

3 to 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing technical role such as implementation, solutions engineering, technical customer success, or professional services, ideally in SaaS, IoT, technology, or logistics.
Bachelor's degree from a 4-year institution, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong technical aptitude, with a track record of quickly learning complex products and troubleshooting issues independently.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and deliver to deadlines, with clear planning and follow-through.
Proven track record of communicating technical concepts clearly and empathetically to non-technical audiences, from day-to-day users to executives.
Solutions-oriented with strong research and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication, presentation, and organizational skills.
Familiarity with Salesforce, Gainsight, Gong or similar GTM tools.
Comfort with a rapidly changing, high-growth environment.

Strong bias towards action , has the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards.
AI First : Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
API and Integration Experience : Experience building with APIs, and/or working with and building integrations.
Project Management Experience : Experience running scoped, project-based customer engagements.
Technical Proficiency : Experience with building deep knowledge of a suite of technical products (bonus points if familiar with integrating hardware with software solutions).

We act as a strategic finance function for complex commercial partner negotiations and work with product leaders to shape their strategy, growth, investment priorities, and financial performance as it scales. What you’ll do
We’re looking for a finance leader to lead Finance & Strategy for Global Partnerships and Startup and Ecosystem Product. You’ll serve as a trusted financial and strategic advisor to the Chief Business Officer and other senior business leaders, connecting commercial decisions to their financial implications.
You’ll lead a team of strategic finance professionals to craft deal analysis and structure recommendations, investment frameworks, and strategic insights that drive long-term economic growth for Stripe. In addition, you will work cross-functionally to ensure disciplined financial planning and forecasting. You’ll develop the team, establish clear priorities, and balance time-sensitive deal support with recurring financial commitments and targeted strategic analysis.
Responsibilities
Lead the financial evaluation of complex product enablement partnerships. Partner with Global Partnerships leaders and Partner Development Managers to evaluate and execute commercial agreements with new and existing partners, bringing an independent financial perspective to negotiation strategy and decisions.
Guide deal economics and investment analysis. Oversee financial modeling, commercial benchmarking, scenario analysis, and investment cases. Translate complex deal structures into clear assessments of financial impact, risks, returns, and commercial trade-offs.
Improve partner economics and performance visibility. Develop data-driven insights to identify strategic and optimization opportunities for Stripe’s partner portfolio. Establish consistent frameworks and metrics to assess partner initiatives and deals.
Build investment cases in support of new business initiatives. Craft financial models in support of Startup and Ecosystem Product initiatives and establish objectives and metrics in partnership with Business and Product leaders.
Actively contribute to org building as part of the F&S leadership team. Help shape and execute F&S priorities, influence and drive cross-functional initiatives, and contribute to culture building of the organization.
Coordinate cross-functional financial recommendations. Work closely with Product and Engineering, Pricing, Strategy and Operations, Treasury Finance, Accounting, and other Finance & Strategy teams to support planning and forecasting activities.
Own the financial planning and forecasting cycle. Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and business reviews for Global Partnerships and Startup and Ecosystem Product areas.
Guide operating expense management. Maintain visibility into resource plans, assess investment and efficiency trade-offs, and surface material changes that require leadership decisions.
Partner on goals, metrics, and performance. Help leaders establish financial objectives and key business metrics for priority businesses and initiatives. Explain material deviations from plan, identify underlying drivers, and recommend actions.
Build and develop a high-performing team. Coach and develop direct reports, set clear expectations, and maintain high standards for analytical quality, business partnership, and execution.

15+ years in strategic finance, commercial finance, product finance, or FP&A, with demonstrated success leading and developing finance teams.

Strong grounding in budgeting, forecasting, headcount and operating expense planning, and business performance management.

Exceptional analytical and financial modeling capabilities, with the ability to connect detailed economics to broader business strategy.
A hands-on leadership style and the judgment to prioritize across urgent transactions, recurring operating commitments, and longer-term strategic work.

What You’ll Do
As technology evolves, so do our tax reporting requirements, especially with the multitude of state and local taxes around the US.  Our state-related indirect obligations and filing requirements continue to grow with the business, and we are looking for someone who can not only maintain but help further build our US sales tax practice in achieving our tax goals.  This individual will need to be versed in indirect tax systems used in compliance, and be able to work with our talented group of engineers who support the state tax function. This position will report to the State & Local Tax Lead.
This position can be office-based in Seattle, South San Francisco, Chicago, New York City, or Remote-US.
Responsibilities
Help establish the direction, goals, and priorities for Stripe’s US indirect tax function, with a strong moral compass and integrity.
Manage and improve state indirect tax compliance systems across our portfolio of companies, and work with the tax reporting and eng teams to ensure coverage on all of our tax filings.  This includes systems used in compliance filings, business registrations, and working with our both tax and non-tax vendors to ensure we are meeting our compliance obligations.
Oversee and run point on special projects impacting US indirect tax systems.
Run models and analyses for state indirect tax planning.
Assist in data collection used in state controversy across different tax types and resolve tax issues.
Monitor SALT developments across the US, including local impacts of federal law.
Proactively identify areas for operational improvements and implement solutions to streamline downstream US indirect tax reporting.

A strong background in tax compliance, specifically US indirect taxes.
Experience in working with teams and engineers in building out US indirect tax infrastructure.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to research and communicate complex technical tax issues clearly to non-tax team members and work effectively across functional teams.

Empathy, humility, and some comedy
You will also likely have (not required):
An advanced degree or professional qualification in tax, accounting, or law (CPA, JD or Master’s degree).
Experience working in a high-growth, rapidly scaling environment.
Industry experience at a multinational organization; experience working in technology, payments, or financial services is a plus.
A willingness to work with a diverse crew of tax nerds who care deeply about Stripe’s tax issues and each other.
